title: Run credential-free artifact persistence in local Kubernetes
description:
As a Plexus platform engineer, I want the local Kubernetes stack to execute credential-free procedure and optimizer artifact persistence, so that the repeatable public demo validates the same supported artifact boundary as hosted deployments.

Feature: Local Kubernetes artifact transfer compatibility

Scenario: Procedure and optimizer artifacts use authorized transfer tickets
Given Plexus is deployed in Docker Desktop Kubernetes with the trusted local control plane and persistent local object storage
When the public demo runs procedure persistence, optimizer output, interruption recovery, and retained verification
Then each migrated artifact is authorized through the existing GraphQL transfer-ticket operation
And bytes are transferred over verified HTTPS
And no direct-S3, insecure transport, authentication, or storage fallback is used for migrated consumers
And evaluation consumers not migrated by PR 513 remain explicitly identified as out of scope

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text:
Additional compatibility scenario found by the live strict suite:

Scenario: Resume optimization from the demo feedback baseline
Given a run-scoped feedback evaluation selected from the retained deterministic seed anchor
When the Kubernetes demo passes that completed evaluation to the optimizer as its recent baseline
Then the evaluation records explicit feedback_start_at and feedback_end_at bounds, the positive lookback days, and the requested maximum item count
And the optimizer resumes the exact frozen cohort without selecting a new one
